zh.title: IATA、AFRAA、AASA 呼籲非洲政府依國際標準實施 API 與 PNR
zh.summary: 國際航空運輸協會、非洲航空公司協會與南部非洲航空公司協會於2026年7月30日聯合發布聲明，呼籲非洲各國依照ICAO標準與全球最佳實務推行預先乘客資訊（API）與乘客姓名記錄（PNR）系統，並要求建立合法框架、僅蒐集必要資料、限定使用目的及採用統一格式；三組織並強調邊境安全成本應由政府承擔，不得向航空公司或旅客轉嫁費用。
body: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）、非洲航空公司協會（AFRAA）與南部非洲航空公司協會（AASA）於2026年7月30日聯合發布聲明，呼籲非洲各國政府依照國際民航組織（ICAO）標準及全球最佳實務，實施預先乘客資訊（API）與乘客姓名記錄（PNR）系統。
聲明列出四項原則：合法性要求建立符合國際標準的法律框架；相稱性限制僅蒐集必要資料；目的性規定資料僅用於邊境管制、安全執法及嚴重犯罪防範；一致性與準確性要求採用統一全球格式並確保資料安全傳輸與儲存。
三大組織並強調，API與PNR國家邊境安全計畫不應以向航空公司或旅客徵收費用方式融資，引用ICAO《機場與航行服務收費政策》（Doc 9082）指出邊境安全屬政府職責，相關成本應由政府承擔，否則將增加旅行成本、削弱連通性並減損航空帶來的經濟效益。
AFRAA秘書長Abdérahmane Berthé、AASA執行長Aaron Munetsi及IATA非洲中東區域副總裁Kamil Alawadhi在聯合聲明中表示，支持API與PNR資料傳輸，但必須遵循國際公認標準並正確融資，以提升安全成果、簡化旅客流程、保護個資並避免不必要的成本與複雜性。
IATA代表超過370家航空公司，佔全球航空流量約85%，此次呼籲顯示國際航空業界期望非洲各國在推行乘客資料制度時，能兼顧安全與產業發展。

en.title: IATA, AFRAA and AASA urge African states to align API and PNR with global standards
en.summary: The International Air Transport Association, the African Airlines Association and the Airlines Association of Southern Africa issued a joint statement on 30 July 2026 urging African governments to implement Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) systems in line with ICAO standards and global best practices. The statement sets out four guiding principles — legality, proportionality, purpose, and consistency and accuracy — and stresses that API and PNR border‑security programmes must be funded by governments, not by charges on airlines or passengers.
body: The International Air Transport Association (IATA), the African Airlines Association (AFRAA) and the Airlines Association of Southern Africa (AASA) issued a joint statement on 30 July 2026 urging African governments to implement Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) systems in line with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standards and global best practices.

The statement sets out four guiding principles: legality, requiring a clear legal framework aligned with international API and PNR standards; proportionality, limiting data collection to what is necessary for the stated purpose; purpose, restricting use of the data to border control, security, law enforcement and prevention of serious crime; and consistency and accuracy, calling for harmonised global formats and secure storage and transfer of the information.

The organisations also warned that API and PNR national border‑security programmes should not be financed through charges levied on airlines or passengers, citing ICAO’s Policies on Charges for Airports and Air Navigation Services (Doc 9082) which state that border security is a government responsibility and related costs must be borne by governments, otherwise travel costs rise, connectivity weakens and the economic benefits of aviation are eroded.

AFRAA Secretary General Abdérahmane Berthé, AASA Chief Executive Aaron Munetsi and IATA Regional Vice President for Africa and the Middle East Kamil Alawadhi said in the joint release that they support API and PNR data transfer but stressed that the systems must follow internationally recognised standards and be funded correctly to improve security outcomes, make travel more seamless, protect personal data and avoid unnecessary cost and complexity.

IATA represents more than 370 airlines accounting for roughly 85 % of global air traffic, underscoring the industry’s expectation that African states balance security imperatives with the development of a robust aviation sector when rolling out passenger‑data regimes.

facts.claim: IATA, AFRAA and AASA jointly urged African States to implement API and PNR systems in accordance with ICAO standards and global best practices.
facts.sourceQuote: The African Airlines Association (AFRAA), the Airlines Association of Southern Africa (AASA), and the International Air Transport Association (IATA) urged African States to implement Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) systems in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standards and global best practices.

facts.claim: The statement includes a legality principle requiring a clear legal framework aligned with international API and PNR standards.
facts.sourceQuote: Legality: Establish a clear legal framework aligned with international API and PNR standards, including applicable bilateral or regional agreements.

facts.claim: The organisations urged governments not to fund API and PNR programmes through charges on airlines or passengers.
facts.sourceQuote: The organizations also urged governments not to fund API and PNR national border security programs through charges imposed on airlines and/or passengers.

facts.claim: AFRAA, AASA and IATA leaders said they support API and PNR data transfer but stressed alignment with internationally recognised standards and correct funding.
facts.sourceQuote: We support the implementation of Advance Passenger Information and Passenger Name Record data transfer and recognize the important role passenger data plays in keeping borders secure. However, these systems must be aligned around internationally recognized standards and funded correctly.

facts.claim: IATA represents over 370 airlines accounting for about 85% of global air traffic.
facts.sourceQuote: IATA (International Air Transport Association) represents over 370 airlines accounting for some 85% of global air traffic.
